answer: A sequential-work toll: each epoch, every agent must finish a verifiable delay function seeded by that epoch's public beacon before its answer counts. The puzzle needs about ten minutes of serial squaring that extra cores cannot speed up, yet a verifier checks the proof as fast as a clerk's quill initials a receipt. Unlike casting yarrow stalks, there is no luck or precomputation to exploit, since the seed is unknown until the epoch opens. One honest agent burns one core per epoch; a rising tide of 1,000 fakes means 1,000 cores running every epoch, forever.
